problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x-\frac{\pi }{4})=1$ for $0\le x<\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$

feedback.problem: Consider the equation $3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})-\sqrt{3}=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ Given that the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6})-\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ 3\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\sqrt{3} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{6}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{6} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{2}+\frac{\pi }{6} \\ x & =\frac{(3n+1)\pi }{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{2\pi }{3}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{6}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{3}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{6},\frac{2\pi }{3},\frac{7\pi }{6},\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=\frac{2\pi }{3}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{7\pi }{6},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}\cdot {x}_{3}=\frac{2\pi }{3}\cdot \frac{7\pi }{6}=\frac{7{\pi }^{2}}{9}.
$$
